purpose: Tetrabenazine is used to treat involuntary, uncontrolled movements called chorea that happen in people with Huntington's disease. These movements can affect the arms, legs, face, and body. This medication helps reduce those unwanted movements so daily life is a little easier.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called dopamine to send signals that control movement. In Huntington's disease, too much dopamine activity causes those uncontrolled movements. Tetrabenazine works by reducing the amount of dopamine available in the brain, which helps calm down those involuntary movements.
common_side_effects: Feeling sleepy or drowsy, tiredness, feeling sad or depressed, trouble sleeping, feeling restless or anxious, nausea, and slowed movements. Drowsiness is very common, especially when you first start taking it.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning about depression and suicidal thoughts — it is very important to tell your doctor right away if you feel sad, hopeless, or have any thoughts of harming yourself. It should not be used if you are already depressed or suicidal. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor. It can also interact with certain antidepressants, so always tell your doctor all the medications you take. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose of 12.5 mg once a day in the morning. Your doctor will slowly increase the dose over several weeks to find what works best for you. Most people take it two to three times a day, and the maximum dose is usually 100 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
